text:
maria_support: Hey team — escalated from account team: enterprise customer on Dedicated started seeing intermittent 401s this morning after we performed a key rotation for our signing key. Error in their logs is 'invalid signature' and their tokens show a kid that should be present in our JWKS. They say it started ~08:20 UTC. Repro steps they provided below. Can someone help triage? :thinking:

alex_platform: thanks — can you paste the raw Authorization header and the kid from the token header (redact token body if needed)? Also which endpoint is failing (hosted vs dedicated internal endpoint)?

maria_support: Pasted (redacted):
- Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InJlZC1rZXktMjAyNi0xIn0....
- Endpoint: https://dedicated-us-west.redwood.example/api/v1/generate
- Customer says failures are ~1 in 10 requests, not all of them.

taylor_eng: intermittent pattern + key rotation -> first suspicion is JWKS caching somewhere in the path (client, our edge, or a CDN) returning an old JWKS without the new key. Two failure modes: 1) token signed with new key but verifier only has old keys -> invalid signature; 2) token has kid that the verifier maps to a different key due to caching/partial update.

akash_sre: also double-check clock skew / exp/iat. If their clock is off and tokens have nbf/exp boundaries we sometimes see weird rejects, but the 'invalid signature' string points to sig validation specifically.

maria_support: Customer included a small trace:
```
[2026-03-13T08:21:03Z] request id=abc123 status=401 reason="invalid signature" verifier=k8s-verifier-3
[2026-03-13T08:21:08Z] request id=abc124 status=200 verifier=k8s-verifier-7
[2026-03-13T08:21:11Z] request id=abc125 status=401 verifier=k8s-verifier-3
```
They see the same token succeed sometimes and fail other times (they repro by replaying the same token).

alex_platform: that log snippet is key — different verifier instances (k8s-verifier-3 vs -7) behave differently. That suggests a rollout where some replicas have stale JWKS cache. Questions: what JWKS cache TTL do we use in the verifier? Are we doing on-demand refresh or background polling?

taylor_eng: our verifier (internal library) caches JWKS for 5m by default and does background refresh on first miss. But if a replica started before the key rotation and never hit a miss it might still hold an in-memory JWKS without the new kid. On rotation we try to publish a key-rotation event to the config bus but if a pod missed it (network flakiness) it can be stale until TTL expiry.

akash_sre: another possibility: an edge/proxy (cloud load balancer or CDN) is caching the JWKS response at the edge with a long TTL (e.g., 1h) because our earlier config lacked Cache-Control headers. If verifier fetches JWKS from the edge URL rather than origin, that would explain mixed behavior depending on which replica fetches from cache.

maria_support: customer says they saw a message from their IdP (third-party SSO) that they rotated keys early this morning too. Could be two rotations together.

taylor_eng: OK plan for triage: 1) confirm which JWKS URI each verifier instance resolves to (internal vs external). 2) fetch the JWKS from origin and compare to each verifier's cached view. 3) check logs for any JWKS fetch errors or unexpected 200 responses with old payload. 4) repro locally by forcing a cached JWKS on one verifier and sending token signed with newly rotated key.

alex_platform: repro commands that helped me in the past:
```
# fetch the raw JWKS from origin (no caching)
curl -sS -H "Cache-Control: no-cache" "https://auth-provider.example/.well-known/jwks.json" | jq . > /tmp/jwks-origin.json

# inspect token header (base64 decode)
echo 'eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6InJlZC1rZXktMjAyNi0xIn0' | base64 --decode | jq .

# verify signature locally (example, requires the correct public key from jwks)
# extract public key (PEM) then:
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature sig.bin data.txt
```
If the origin JWKS contains the kid and the verifying replica's cache doesn't, that's our smoking gun.

maria_support: I fetched the JWKS endpoint for the customer with no-cache and it shows both old and new keys present (new kid is "red-key-2026-1"). I also asked them to hit /health on each verifier pod and we got back which JWKS hash they currently have cached. Two pods have the old hash.

akash_sre: confirms: this is a classic partial-rollout cache-stale problem. Fix options: immediate mitigations and longer-term fixes.

maria_support: customer is asking for an immediate mitigation — they are sensitive to downtime.

akash_sre: Immediate mitigations (we should coordinate with customer):
- Force JWKS cache invalidation on all verifier pods (restart pods or trigger a config bus refresh).
- If restart is risky, send a cache-busting GET from each pod to the origin JWKS with Cache-Control: no-cache (we have an admin endpoint that will trigger JWKS reload in-place: POST /admin/keys/reload).
- Ensure our load balancer / CDN isn't serving stale JWKS: purge edge cache for /.well-known/jwks.json if it's being proxied.

alex_platform: longer-term mitigations:
- On key rollover, include both old and new keys concurrently in JWKS for an overlap window (we already try to but need to confirm all key-rotation flows do this).
- Make verifier code proactively refresh on key miss synchronously instead of relying on background polling. If a token arrives with kid X and our cache lacks it, attempt immediate fetch and retry verification once.
- Add exponential backoff + jitter on JWKS fetch to avoid thundering herd, but ensure at least one replica does a forced refresh on rotation events.
- Add an explicit rotation webhook from the control plane to verifiers to invalidate caches.

taylor_eng: small code snippet to make replication of the bug easier (NodeJS-ish pseudocode):
```
// simulate stale cache
const cached = loadCachedJWKS() // returns only old keys
const token = getExampleTokenSignedWithNewKey()
if (!cached.has(token.header.kid)) {
  // current code: accept stale until TTL expires
  // proposed: fetchNow() and retry verification
}
```

maria_support: customer asked for repro steps they can run to prove issue fixed after we apply mitigation. Suggested steps I sent them: 1) get a token signed with new kid (we can mint one for them), 2) hit the dedicated endpoint multiple times across different backends, 3) confirm 200 consistently, 4) if any 401s, capture the verifier pod name and logs.

akash_sre: I'm going to run a coordinated reload across the cluster now and purge the CDN entry. Will update here when done.

jwt-bot: automated message: keys/reload job queued to cluster/redwood-dedicated-us-west at 2026-03-13T09:05:12Z.

akash_sre: done with reload and CDN purge. Verified all pods now report JWKS hash matching origin. Customer asked to retry.

maria_support: they retried and confirm 0/200 requests failing now after many replays. They also requested a postmortem and a follow-up PR to harden rotation.

alex_platform: action items:
- alex_platform: open PR to change verifier on-miss behavior -> fetch+retry (small change)
- taylor_eng: audit key-rotation paths to ensure we always publish new key to JWKS before switching signing key; confirm overlap window policy and add tests.
- akash_sre: add a rotation webhook that triggers /admin/keys/reload on all verifier pods and a CDN purge step in rotation runbook.
- maria_support: coordinate customer follow-up and deliver postmortem.

maria_support: thanks all — customer happy for now. tagging owners: @alex_platform @taylor_eng @akash_sre. :thumbsup:

# Notes/lessons learned (kept inline for PM/postmortem):
- Intermittent 401s post-rotation often mean partial cache-stale, not necessarily a crypto bug.
- Verify where JWKS is fetched from (origin vs proxied) and ensure cache headers are explicit.
- Consider synchronous fetch-on-miss to avoid user-visible transient failures during rotation.
- When debugging, always compare the actual JWKS seen by the failing verifier to the origin JWKS.
- Repro tips: use Cache-Control: no-cache, base64-decode JWT header to inspect kid, and attempt verification locally with openssl if necessary.

End of thread.
